notes: Phase 1 Step 3 (LLM API candidate labeling) for Pass 5 (CWE-89 SQL Injection) only, against the piccolo_vuln source tree; the tree matches the CodeQL DB (piccolo-db) creation sha e4946d858e1aae1a9a4cf7714957d07983d94cde, and every CSV file:line cited in evidence was re-read from that tree during labeling.

Coverage: all 398 source-candidate rows + 221 sink-candidate rows = 619 candidates, each assigned to exactly one semantic group; 20 source-side groups + 22 sink-side groups (42 label entries). Per-row assignments are in labels/labels_raw_pass5.json. Duplicate CSV rows (identical node/callable/arg/file/line) are recorded there and covered once.

This run is an in-context LLM labeling session (model glm-5.3 operating the Claude Code agent harness); no external LLM API calls were made. 12 analysis batches were processed; per-batch scope and row counts are recorded in labels_raw_pass5.json.

Mixed groups carry a representative signature in this file; Phase 2 library generation should expand per-row signatures from labels_raw_pass5.json (e.g. snk-01 covers fetch/execute/cursor on both engines; src-01 covers ~61 distinct CLI command functions).
pass 1 block: present with zero entries solely to satisfy the labels_schema.json 'passes contains pass_id=1' constraint; no pass-1 labeling was performed in this run.

Threat model: piccolo is an ORM library with NO HTTP surface (confirmed in detection.json: no web framework imports; the external-input frameworks are the local `piccolo` targ CLI, interactive prompts, files, env). The ORM's public API (Table.raw, WhereRaw, SelectRaw, Alter DDL methods, Savepoint names, clause delegates) is therefore modeled as the trust boundary through which an embedding application's attacker-influenced data enters SQL construction (api_param family).

Key semantic findings: (1) QueryString is a genuine parameterized compiler - values passed as QueryString args become $n/? bound parameters and never enter SQL text (querystring.py:124-192); the bound_params sink family is labeled none/fp accordingly. (2) The raw-SQL text channels are Table.raw/WhereRaw/SelectRaw argument 0 (source+sink pair src-07/snk-15) - in-library call sites all pass literal templates. (3) The DDL/savepoint identifier channels interpolate names UNQUOTED or quoted-but-unescaped with no allowlist (alter.py:36/117/188, postgres.py:239, sqlite.py:313/416, schema.py) - labeled source tp (src-08) + sink tp (snk-04a/09/10). (4) LIMIT/OFFSET have a proven isinstance(int) guard (src-15 sanitizer). (5) Second-order channel: DB-reflected table/column names are re-interpolated into SQL text (PRAGMA index_list, ROWID lookup, FROM clauses) - summary family src-19. (6) No SQL-syntax-context validation or identifier whitelist exists anywhere in the library; no sanitizer other than the limit/offset int guard and the QueryString bound-args channel itself. (7) Engine-layer receiver-collision noise identified and excluded: postgres.py:41 cursor.fetch(batch_size), error-message f-strings (objects.py:334, query/base.py:426).

Independence: PyVul ground truth, fix commits, CVE listings and external vulnerability advisories were NOT read; vendor-supplied audit artifacts inside the tree were excluded per detection.json runNote. No source files, databases, extraction results or Augur files were modified.

entries.rationale: The ORM's raw-SQL text boundary: Table.raw(sql, *args) (table.py:964-979) and WhereRaw(sql, *args) (combination.py:109-131) directly make the caller's sql string the QueryString template that engines compile and execute. The *args (positions 2+) ride the safe bound channel, but argument 1 (sql) is executed as SQL structure. This is the classic channel through which an embedding application that concatenates request data into raw SQL becomes injectable - the library itself documents 'use with caution!'. In-library call sites all pass literal templates (schema generate, table_exists), so exploitability requires an embedding app; the channel itself is genuinely attacker-reachable in the ORM trust model.
evidence: piccolo/table.py:964 'def raw(cls, sql: str, *args)' -> :979 Raw(querystring=QueryString(sql, *args))
piccolo/table.py:967 docstring 'Execute raw SQL queries on the underlying engine - use with caution!'
piccolo/columns/combination.py:112 WhereRaw.__init__(self, sql, *args) -> :131 self.querystring = QueryString(sql, *args)
SelectRaw.__init__ carries the same shape (select.py:58 QueryString(sql, *args)) and is captured on the sink side (snk-15)

entries.rationale: Public ORM/DDL API parameters that are interpolated into DDL/SQL statement text rather than bound parameters: Alter.rename_table(new_name) -> f'RENAME TO {new_name}' (alter.py:36, UNQUOTED); Alter.rename_column(column, new_name) -> f'RENAME COLUMN "{col}" TO "{new_name}"' (alter.py:63, quoted but not escaped); Alter.set_column_type(old, new, using_expression) -> USING {using_expression} interpolated verbatim (alter.py:117, UNQUOTED); Alter.drop_constraint(constraint_name) -> f'DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS {name}' (alter.py:188, UNQUOTED); Alter.set_schema(schema_name) -> SetSchema DDL (alter.py:560); Savepoint(name)/rollback_to(savepoint_name) -> f'SAVEPOINT {name}' / f'ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT {name}' (postgres.py:239/133, sqlite.py:416/313, UNQUOTED). No identifier allowlist or escaping exists on any of these paths. Attacker reachability requires the embedding app or CLI to pass request-influenced strings; in-library callers pass developer/migration-defined names, so classification is tp for the channel with that scope caveat.
